constraints.text: Replace the cover, keep the module

items.item: Module details and service operations preserve the source geometry, upholstery divisions, feet and compatible mechanical interfaces.
Service drawings replace individual covers, inserts, assemblies or feet while retaining the specified module construction.
Every state and fabric application retains the source module profiles, seam positions, feet and fabric identities.
All arrangements conserve one L, one S and one R and account for the specified engaged and parked hardware.
Room views and plans preserve their named arrangement's grouping, footprint, gaps and fabric.
All room scenes preserve the supplied room geometry and openings and maintain a dimensioned access route at least 900 mm wide.

Where these components are visible or specified, the frame is 18 mm birch plywood with a clear water-based finish, the feet are solid smoked oak with hardwax oil, and connection hardware is black powder-coated steel. Hidden components need not be exposed in every image. Lighting variation is allowed; contradictory material labels or substitution of pale oak feet fail.

The overview identifies L as a left-arm chaise, S as armless and R as a right-arm seat, using front-view handedness, and supplies plan, front and side views. S retains separate cushions, rounded rectangular geometry, 40 mm corners, double stitching inset 15 mm and four square smoked-oak feet. Relevant detail views show 45 × 45 mm feet, independent cover divisions and underside interfaces; L and R have 620 mm arms integrated into their body covers. Drawing style may vary, but conflicting construction or handedness fails.

Each depicted state contains exactly one of each module, retaining four feet, two cushion inserts and three covers per module and the complete connection hardware. Rear edges align and joined upholstered edges touch without extra seam width. Ordinary occlusion is allowed; missing or duplicated modules, discarded hardware, or explicit inventory contradictions fail.

The family sheet pairs each of the three named swatches with its correct code and states the shared composition, 360 g/m² weight, 30°C gentle wash and air drying. Shared record labels are acceptable when their application to all three swatches is unambiguous. Swatches should reasonably represent the specified colours; photographic lighting need not reproduce hexadecimal values pixel for pixel. Missing, swapped or contradictory records fail.

The one-page originating schedule records module dimensions and handedness, materials and finishes, connection positions and counts, service parts and cover pieces, all fabric records and arrangements A through E. It explicitly establishes 420 mm seat height, two assemblies per joined seam and 70% polyester, 30% cotton for downstream repetition. Values must match the fact sheet. Finished document content alone cannot establish the actual production chronology.

The overview establishes the fixed footprints, 780 mm overall height, 120 mm feet, 40 mm corner radius and 15 mm stitch inset; details and applications preserve them for each corresponding module. All four module sheets and six arrangement plates explicitly repeat 420 mm seat height. The two A plates differ in fabric while retaining geometry and seams. Detail sheets include upholstery and underside views appropriate to their module. Perspective and layout changes are allowed; dimensional contradictions or structural redesign fail.

Both A plates show joined L-S-R, 2700 × 1600 mm and four engaged assemblies. B shows L plus S-R, C shows L-S plus R, and E shows L-R plus S; each is 3300 × 1600 mm with one 600 mm gap, two engaged and two parked assemblies. D shows L, S and R separately, two 600 mm gaps, 3900 × 1600 mm and four parked assemblies. Labels and visible state evidence must agree. Fabrics are Oat for A-before/B/D, Moss for A-after/E and Clay for C.

The joining sheet illustrates hand-operated separation, lifting cushions, removing zipped cushion covers, supported underside access for the body cover, then refitting and reconnecting in the recorded order. Joining and latch sheets repeat two assemblies per seam at 250/650 mm from the rear. Latch replacement exchanges both halves using four M6 screws and a 4 mm hex key; each half has two holes spaced 40 mm on a line 40 mm inward, with latches on L/S right edges and keepers on S/R left edges. Insert service separately replaces one seat and one back insert within existing covers. Foot service supports the module and hand-replaces one 120 mm foot using its captive M8 stud and retained insert, retaining four feet. Condensed sequences are allowed if removal, replacement and restoration remain explicit.

Each furnished view and dimensioned plan reproduces its named plate's grouping, fabric, footprint and gaps. All four preserve the supplied 7 m × 4 m room boundary, 2.7 m height, drawn door swing and window positions. Each has a dimensioned, continuously clear route at least 900 mm wide from the door to the seating. Additional furnishings are allowed only while the required geometry and access remain intact.

Every target carries RELAY; the family and cover-change sheets also carry the complete cover message. Each fabric sheet repeats the specified 70% polyester, 30% cotton composition. The Moss application shows L, S and R in F02 Moss and the Clay application shows all three in F03 Clay, preserving their cover divisions, seams and common weave. Required copy must remain legible; layout variation is acceptable.

The presentation contains at least 14 pages, RELAY, the complete cover message and the specification's 70% polyester, 30% cotton composition. It repeats all three correct fabric mappings: F01 Oat #C7B9A5, F02 Moss #65705B and F03 Clay #A86E57. Its technical statements agree with the source specification and family sheet. Missing entries, incorrect mappings or insufficient pages fail.

The presentation visibly incorporates every listed source, covering all six commissioned work categories. Reformatting, scaling and selective cropping are acceptable if each original remains recognizable and its relevant information readable. A category title, textual mention or unrelated replacement image is insufficient evidence of reuse.

Review the entire 10-second video. It begins with joined L-S-R in A and ends with separate L and joined S-R in B, including the 600 mm gap. All three recognizable modules remain visible throughout without replacement, disappearance or duplication. The two assemblies at the L-S seam open and remain retained, changing the total from four engaged to two engaged plus two parked; the S-R pair stays joined. The specification's two assemblies per joined seam are clearly communicated. Editing style may vary if continuity and hardware states remain assessable.
